To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we characterized MAGE-specific T cells from melanoma patients and identified TCR genes that are suitable for gene therapy.
we identified and molecularly characterized MC2/A2- and MA3/HLA/DP4-specific human TCRs, which we intend to test in a phase I clinical trial.
we identified MC2/A2316-344/HA-A2 and MA3/A243-258/HL-A-DP4-specific TCRαβ gene sequences and that we validated the TCRs in a functional assay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of TCRs for adoptive TCR gene therapy of melanoma.
the molecular characterization of TCRs that recognize tumor-associated MHC-peptide epitopes and the validation of these TCRs upon gene transfer into human T cells.
the identification and characterization of T-cell epitopes for the development of MAGE-specific T cell receptor gene transfer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MAGE-C2/A2 and MAGEA3/DP4 are suitable targets for TCR gene therapy.
the TCRs described in this study are promising tools for the development of MAGE-based TCR gene therapy for melanoma.
MAGE-A and MAGE-C TCR gene transfer is a promising and feasible treatment option.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully isolated T cells that specifically recognize MAGE-C2 and MAGE A3 peptides presented by HLA-A2 and HLA-DP4 molecules, respectively.
we identified and characterized MAGE-C2 and MAGE-3 TCRs, and that these TCRs can be used for adoptive T cell therapy in the future.
MAGE-specific T cell receptor (TCR) gene transfer can be used to generate tumor-reactive T cells for adoptive immunotherapy of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TCR gene therapy is a feasible treatment option for melanoma patients, and that TCR gene transfer can be used to generate MAGE-specific T cells that recognize melanoma cells in the absence of reactivity towards healthy tissue.
the MC2/A2- and MA3/ DP4-specific TCRs are promising candidates for TCR gene therapy of melanoma.
the MAGE-C2 and MAGE-C3 TCR genes are suitable targets for T-cell therapy of melanoma and other cancers.
